name: קְהָת
summary: The second of Levi’s three sons (with Gershon and Merari), who went down to Egypt with Jacob and lived 133 years; his sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, and through Amram he was grandfather of Aaron and Moses, so the priests are of his line, and Korah son of Izhar too. His sons, the Kohathites, camped south of the Dwelling, kept the ark, table, lampstand and altars, and carried them on the shoulder, setting out “carrying the sanctuary” (Num 10:21); they received the first lot of cities. Scripture gives no reason for the name, and its letters form no other Hebrew word; it may be formed like יִקְּהָה “obedience” (Gen 49:10) without its first letter, as the Sabaean noun qht “obedience, command” is, so “obedience”, but that is uncertain.

evidence.note: “The sons of Levi: Gershon, קְהָת and Merari”, among those who came into Egypt with Jacob.
“The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were 133 years.”
Amram took Jochebed and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
“Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi.”
The clans of the sons of Kohath camp on the south side of the Dwelling and keep the ark, table, lampstand, altars and the vessels of the holy place.
“This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting: the most holy things.”
After Aaron and his sons cover the holy things, the sons of Kohath come to carry them, but must not touch them and die.
To the sons of Kohath Moses gave no wagons: they carried on the shoulder.
“The Kohathites set out, carrying the sanctuary”: the gentilic of the name.
The first lot came out for the clans of the Kohathite, the priests among them.
The sons of Kohath in David’s divisions of the Levites.
The Hebrew word the name may be formed like: וְלוֹ יִקְּהַת עַמִּים, “and to him the obedience of the peoples”.
The same word: the eye that “despises obedience (לִיקֲּהַת) to a mother”.

evidence.locator: pp. 144–145, WQH (verb obey, order, command; nouns qh, qht obedience, authority, command)
evidence.note: Sabaean wqh “obey; command”, whose noun qht drops the first letter and has the name’s three letters.

note: TIPNR files the gentilic קְהָתִי under this record too, but it is a word of the qehat entry (s.ap.aj), so this name claims s.ap.ai only; see the qehat entry's note. The database keys the name under root קהל (BDB's alphabetical placement); the name is linked to the root key קהת. The meaning “obedience” is a possibility from the Sabaean noun and Hebrew יִקְּהָה, not shown by any verse; Kohath was born before Israel went down to Egypt (Gen 46:11), and no verse explains why he was so named.
